frontier.hypothesis: The halfword index `idx2` can be made a MULTI-BLOCK pseudo at zero instruction cost, which hands DA the target's allocation and therefore distance 0.
frontier.mechanism: DA already emits the target's exact instruction sequence; its only defect is that local-alloc claims $s0 for the block-local `idx2` before global-alloc ever sees `idx`. A pseudo referenced in two basic blocks has reg_basic_block < 0 and is invisible to local-alloc, so it would instead be ranked against `idx` by global.c:allocno_compare — where `idx` (24 refs across 29 insns in DA) beats `idx2` (9 refs across 27) and takes $s0, leaving $s1 for idx2 exactly as the target has it. The only shape tried so far, `idx2 = idx << 1;` at the loop top (DC), costs one instruction because the sll leaves the first jal's delay slot empty.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate C bodies in which the halfword index is genuinely read or written in a SECOND basic block without adding an instruction — the loop-bottom block (where j is incremented and tested), the outer-loop tail, or a shape in which the inner loop maintains the halfword index rather than the slot index — and sandbox each on the DA chassis (tmp/grind/func_800645B0/s6/sweep20.py has the DA body factored for this).

frontier.hypothesis: A second block-local call-crossing quantity in the DA if-body would claim $s0 ahead of `idx2`, or `idx2` can be steered to $s1 by a register suggestion.
frontier.mechanism: This is the other resolution of the H32 contradiction. local-alloc.c:1648 ranks block-local quantities by floor_log2 (n_refs) * n_refs * size / (death - birth), and find_free_reg tries SUGGESTED registers before scanning reg_alloc_order (local-alloc.c:2205-2215, qty_phys_copy_sugg then qty_phys_sugg). A quantity tied by a copy to a hard register gets such a suggestion; nothing in the current body gives `idx2` one.
frontier.next_probe: Read local-alloc.c's construction of qty_phys_copy_sugg / qty_phys_sugg in block_alloc, then run the DA build under BB2_SUGG_DEBUG / BB2_QTY_DEBUG (tmp/grind/func_800645B0/s6/dumpi.sh, adding the env vars) to see the exact quantity ranking and the used/first_used sets find_free_reg scans for idx2; isolate this function's slice of the log by matching the insn UIDs already extracted in dump_DA/f_lreg.txt.

frontier.hypothesis: The loop-top `addu` can be made to become READY last, so it is emitted first even WITH the birthing lift — which would let the CA chassis (whose allocation is already the target's) reach 0 without touching reg_n_sets.
frontier.mechanism: The lift makes insn 38 the highest-priority ready insn, so the backward scheduler picks it the instant it becomes ready, and it becomes ready as soon as its only in-block dependent (the sllv, insn 43) is scheduled. If the loop-top block contained a second, later-scheduled consumer of `idx`, insn 38 could not be picked until the final slot and would be emitted first regardless of its priority.
frontier.next_probe: Determine whether any instruction the target already has in that block — the D_800A3444 load, the `and`, or the j increment that sits in the branch delay slot — can be made to depend on `idx` without adding an instruction, and measure each spelling on the CA chassis; dump_CA/f_sched.txt is the baseline to diff the ready lists against.
